UX
● UI/UX design agency

UI/UX design that people find easy to use.

Research, flows and screens for websites and apps, tested with real users and built into a design system your team can keep using.

See the work

In short

UI/UX design is the work of understanding how people use a website or app, then designing the flows and screens that make it easy to get done what they came to do.

Monday Marketing Company (MMC) designs websites and apps for D2C, B2B and education brands, and builds the design system behind them.

  • Start with usersInterviews and analytics show what people actually do.
  • Design the journeyFlows and screens shaped around the task, not the org chart.
  • A system that scalesReusable components so new pages stay consistent.
Where interfaces go wrong

Five ways UX goes wrong.

Most usability problems are built in early. Each stage below is where they start, and how we design them out.

  1. 1
    Stage 1 of 5Understand the users

    Designing for what the team assumes.

    Teams know their product too well. Real users use it differently, and find different things hard.

    What we do

    We interview users and study analytics, so design starts from what people actually do and where they get stuck.

    Research
  2. 2
    Stage 2 of 5Map the journey

    Arranging pages by how the business is organised.

    Users think in tasks, not in departments. A structure that follows the org chart makes tasks harder.

    What we do

    We map the key journeys and rebuild the structure around the tasks people came to do.

    User flows
  3. 3
    Stage 3 of 5Design the screens

    Jumping straight to polished visuals.

    Visual polish on a weak flow only hides the problem. Structure comes before style.

    What we do

    We move from wireframes to polished screens, checking each against the task it must support.

    Wireframes and UI
  4. 4
    Stage 4 of 5Test before you build

    Finding out about problems after launch.

    Fixing a problem in a prototype costs a fraction of fixing it in a live product.

    What we do

    We build clickable prototypes and test them with real users before development starts.

    Prototype and usability testing
  5. 5
    Stage 5 of 5Build a system

    Designing every page from scratch.

    Without shared components, sites drift and every change takes longer.

    What we do

    We build a design system of reusable components and rules that your designers and developers can keep using.

    Design systems
What we read

Four numbers that show whether an interface is working.

Read with real users, not guessed.

Task completionWhether people finish what they came to do.
Time on taskHow long the main tasks take.
Drop-off pointsWhere people give up.
ConsistencyWhether pages and components behave the same way.

Common questions

Questions about UI/UX design.

What is UI/UX design?

UI/UX design is the work of understanding how people use a website or app, then designing the flows and screens that make it easy to get done what they came to do. UX is how it works; UI is how it looks.

How does UI/UX design work with MMC?

We research the users, map flows, wireframe and design screens, test clickable prototypes with real users, and package everything as a design system.

What does UI/UX design cost?

We quote per project, after a call, once the scope is clear: what you need, how much of it, and what it has to connect to. The scope and the fee are agreed in writing before work starts.

Do you guarantee results?

No. Nobody can guarantee a conversion lift from design alone. We commit to research, testing with real users and a clear design system, and honest reporting.

Who is UI/UX design for?

Teams building or fixing a website or app. Not only D2C. We work with D2C, B2B and education brands, and set the work up differently for each: D2C on contribution margin and repeat purchase, B2B on the cost of a qualified lead, education on enquiries, visits and admissions.

What do you need from us?

Access to your product or site, analytics, your brand assets, and a few users or customers we can talk to.
